# Qodalis CLI plugin development

Guide for building plugins for Qodalis CLI: commands for the browser terminal (web plugins) and commands served by the Node, .NET and Python servers (server plugins). Full documentation: https://cli.qodalis.com/docs.

## Overview

### Architecture

Qodalis CLI is a web terminal whose commands are command processors registered through modules.

The browser engine (`@qodalis/cli`, wrapped by `@qodalis/angular-cli`, `@qodalis/react-cli` and `@qodalis/vue-cli`) parses each line, finds the processor whose `command` (or alias) matches and calls its `processCommand`. Shared contracts live in `@qodalis/cli-core`. A server (Node, .NET or Python) can contribute more commands: the terminal lists them from `/api/v1/qcli/commands` and runs them through `/api/v1/qcli/execute`.

### Packages

The npm packages a plugin author uses and what each contains.

| Package | Contents |
| --- | --- |
| `@qodalis/cli-core` | Interfaces (`ICliCommandProcessor`, `ICliExecutionContext`, `ICliModule`, `ICliInputReader`), types, utilities |
| `@qodalis/cli` | The framework-agnostic engine (`CliEngine`) |
| `@qodalis/angular-cli`, `@qodalis/react-cli`, `@qodalis/vue-cli` | Framework wrappers |
| `@qodalis/create-cli-plugin` | Plugin scaffolding tool |
| `@qodalis/cli-server-abstractions` (npm), `qodalis-cli-server-abstractions` (PyPI), `Qodalis.Cli.Abstractions` (NuGet) | Server plugin contracts |

## Web plugins

### Scaffold a plugin

Create a plugin project with `@qodalis/create-cli-plugin`, interactively or with flags.

```bash
npx -y @qodalis/create-cli-plugin@latest --name weather --description "Weather forecasts" --processor-name Weather
```

Inside a web-cli checkout it creates `packages/plugins/<name>` and adds the path alias to `tsconfig.base.json`; elsewhere it creates a standalone `qodalis-cli-<name>` project, installs its dependencies and builds with `tsup`. The name is lowercase without the `cli-` prefix; the package is `@qodalis/cli-<name>`.

### Command processors

A command is a class implementing `ICliCommandProcessor` from `@qodalis/cli-core`.

```typescript
import {
    CliProcessCommand,
    DefaultLibraryAuthor,
    ICliCommandProcessor,
    ICliExecutionContext,
} from '@qodalis/cli-core';

export class CliGreetCommandProcessor implements ICliCommandProcessor {
    command = 'greet';
    description = 'Greets someone';
    author = DefaultLibraryAuthor;
    version = '1.0.0';
    parameters = [
        { name: 'loud', aliases: ['l'], description: 'Shout', required: false, type: 'boolean' },
    ];

    async processCommand(command: CliProcessCommand, context: ICliExecutionContext): Promise<void> {
        const name = command.positionals?.[0] ?? 'world';
        const text = `Hello, ${name}!`;
        context.writer.writeln(command.args['loud'] ? text.toUpperCase() : text);
    }
}
```

`command.positionals` holds the arguments split like a shell, `command.args` the flags. Look up every member with `qcli_api ICliCommandProcessor` and `qcli_api CliProcessCommand`.

### Sub-commands

Nest processors in `processors` to build `tool action` style commands.

```typescript
this.processors = [
    {
        command: 'new',
        description: 'Generate a value',
        processCommand: async (command, context) => {
            context.writer.writeln(crypto.randomUUID());
        },
    },
];
```

The parent's `processCommand` runs when no sub-command matches; it usually prints help.

### Writing output

`context.writer` (`ICliTerminalWriter`) prints text, colours, tables and status lines.

```typescript
context.writer.writeln('plain line');
context.writer.writeSuccess('Saved');
context.writer.writeWarning('Nothing to do');
context.writer.writeError('Failed');
```

Use `context.spinner` and `context.progressBar` for long operations and honour `context.signal` so Ctrl+C stops the work.

### Reading input

`context.reader` (`ICliInputReader`) asks the user for text, passwords, confirmations and choices.

```typescript
const name = await context.reader.readLine('Name: ');
if (name === null) {
    return; // cancelled with Ctrl+C or Escape
}
const sure = await context.reader.readConfirm('Continue?', true);
const color = await context.reader.readSelect('Colour', [
    { label: 'Red', value: 'red' },
    { label: 'Blue', value: 'blue' },
]);
```

Every method resolves to `null` when the user cancels.

### Modules

A plugin exports an `ICliModule` that bundles its processors, services and translations.

```typescript
import { API_VERSION, ICliModule } from '@qodalis/cli-core';
import { CliGreetCommandProcessor } from './lib/processors/cli-greet-command-processor';

export const greetModule: ICliModule = {
    apiVersion: API_VERSION,
    name: '@qodalis/cli-greet',
    processors: [new CliGreetCommandProcessor()],
    translations: {
        fr: { 'cli.greet.description': 'Salue quelqu’un' },
    },
};
```

Modules whose `apiVersion` is below the runtime's `API_VERSION` are rejected, so use the constant.

### Registering a module

Hosts pass modules to the terminal; there is no processors-only registration.

```typescript
// Angular
providers: [resolveCliModuleProvider(greetModule)]
// React / Vue
<Cli modules={[greetModule]} />
// Plain TypeScript
engine.registerModule(greetModule);
```

A plugin can also be loaded at runtime from its IIFE bundle (`umd/index.js`), which calls `bootCliModule(module)`.

### Testing

Plugin tests are Jasmine specs in `src/tests/*.spec.ts`.

Run them with `pnpm nx test <name>` inside web-cli (ChromeHeadless, no watch) or with the test script of a standalone project. Test the processor through `processCommand` with a fake execution context, covering invalid input and cancellation.

## Server plugins

### Node.js processor

Server commands extend `CliCommandProcessor` from `@qodalis/cli-server-abstractions` and return text.

```typescript
import { CliCommandProcessor, CliProcessCommand } from '@qodalis/cli-server-abstractions';

export class GreetProcessor extends CliCommandProcessor {
    command = 'greet';
    description = 'Greets someone';

    async handleAsync(command: CliProcessCommand): Promise<string> {
        return `Hello, ${command.value ?? 'world'}!`;
    }
}

const { builder } = createCliServer({});
builder.addProcessor(new GreetProcessor());
```

### .NET processor

Server commands derive from `CliCommandProcessor` and implement `HandleAsync`.

```csharp
public class GreetProcessor : CliCommandProcessor
{
    public override string Command { get; set; } = "greet";
    public override string Description { get; set; } = "Greets someone";

    public override Task<string> HandleAsync(CliProcessCommand command, CancellationToken cancellationToken = default)
        => Task.FromResult($"Hello, {command.Value ?? "world"}!");
}

builder.Services.AddCli(cli => cli.AddProcessor<GreetProcessor>());
```

### Python processor

Server commands subclass `CliCommandProcessor` from `qodalis_cli_server_abstractions`.

```python
from qodalis_cli_server_abstractions import CliCommandProcessor


class GreetProcessor(CliCommandProcessor):
    command = "greet"
    description = "Greets someone"

    async def handle_async(self, command, cancellation_event=None) -> str:
        return f"Hello, {command.value or 'world'}!"


builder.add_processor(GreetProcessor())
```

### Server modules

Group related server processors in a module and register it once.

Node: `builder.addModule(new MyModule())`; Python: `builder.add_module(MyModule())`; .NET: `cli.AddModule(new MyModule())`. A module has a name, a version and its processors.

## Recipes

### Ask before a destructive action

Confirm with `readConfirm` and stop when the answer is not yes.

```typescript
const ok = await context.reader.readConfirm(`Delete ${file}?`, false);
if (!ok) {
    context.writer.writeWarning('Cancelled');
    return;
}
```

### Expose a command to AI assistants

Server commands become MCP tools when the server enables its MCP endpoint.

Enable it with `createCliServer({ mcp: true })` (Node), `CliServerOptions(mcp=True)` (Python) or `cli.AddMcp()` (.NET), then connect Claude Code with `claude mcp add qcli -e QCLI_URL=http://localhost:8047 -e QCLI_TOKEN=<token> -- npx -y @qodalis/mcp-cli`.
